Leon Draisaitl leads all 529 skaters in our wins-added measure, which counts how much each goal moved his team's chance of winning, and he has done it with 20 goals in 22 games. The interesting part is that this isn't only hot shooting. His own chances have jumped to 1.62 expected goals per 60 minutes (the quality of his shots, scaled to ice time), from 1.02 last season. He's getting to better ice than he did a year ago, then finishing at his usual elite rate on top.

Usual elite, plus a bit. He's shooting 24% against 19% last season, and Edmonton has scored 23.9 more goals than expected with him on the ice, so the goal pace sits above even his ceiling. Our numbers expect it to settle, not collapse. The rest of his game hasn't needed luck: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season, carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries. He's on a nine-game point streak, but the shot quality is the part to watch.
